name: Chinese roofs and brackets
_about: The pieces a Chinese hall is roofed with, side by side. A rectangular roof is any of the engine's forms bent into the JUJIA section (`lo`, `hi`: the slope at the eave and at the ridge -- flat below, steep above) with its corners turned UP and swept OUT (`upturn`, `flare`): the hip roof (wudian, the highest rank), the hip-and-gable (xieshan, the gablet form), the overhanging gable (xuanshan) and the pyramid (cuanjian). A ROUND roof is a dome whose profile is `jujia`: a pavilion's cone, or with an `oculus` the ring of roof round the drum of the tier above. Last, a row of `dougong` bracket sets on an architrave.

wudian._about: hip roof (wudian): four slopes, the ridge shortened by the hips

xieshan._about: hip-and-gable (xieshan): a hip to half its height, a gable over it

round pavilion._about: a round pavilion's roof: the jujia section turned

round tier._about: one tier of a round hall's roof: the jujia ring from the eave in to the drum above

tier drum._about: the drum of the next tier, standing on the roof where it has narrowed to its radius
